To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the propagation of the plasmons in the chain of electrolytic spheres can be described by a model which takes into account retarded near-, medium- and far-field dipole-dipole interaction between spheres and which allows to calculate the propagation of plasmons with arbitrary polarization in the whole range of the plasmonic wave vector.
collective surface plasmon-polarity modes can exist in periodic ionic structures, and these modes can be used to study the properties of these structures.

the collective surface plasmopolaritons in ionic chains can be described by the model of self-sustained propagation in the case of a weakly damped plasmon-polarity mode, and that this model can be useful for understanding the mechanisms of the saltatory nerve conduction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new approach to the description of the collective surface waves in the 1D ionic structures, which can be used for the interpretation of various phenomena of the collective ion transport in biological tissues.
a theoretical description of the propagation of collective surface plasmons, called plasmons-polaritons or surface plasmon-pole waves (SPWs), in infinite periodic chain of electrolyte spheres.
a new class of the plasmonic structures, which may be useful for various technological applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the plasmon polariton model is able to describe the saltatory nerve axon conduction in the framework of the collective wave propagation concept.
the plasmonpolariton model of ionic conduction can be considered as a promising candidate for description of saltatory nerve conduction.
the plasmon model of saltatory conduction is a viable one and deserves further development and experimental verification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the collective surface plasmone in the chain of the electrolyte spheres can propagate without any losses at least in a wide range of wave vectors.
the plasmon model can be used to describe collective surface excitations in periodic structures of ionic spheres, such as the nerve fiber, with a high level of accuracy.
the propagation of the collective plasmons in the periodic ionic chain is possible in a wide range of the ion concentration and the chain parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasmon polaritons can be used as a new type of the collective excitations in the ionic structure.
the propagation of collective surface plasmons, called plasmons-polaritons can be realized in ionic chains with a complete cancellation of irradiative and friction losses.
collective plasmon-polyaritons in periodic ionic structure are weakly damped, and the propagation range can be limited only by residual Ohmic losses.
